subject: Packaging & migration credits proposal for Packageloader — pricing alignment
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@packageloader.com>, Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@packageloader.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging & migration credits proposal for Packageloader — pricing alignment

Elena / Ben,

Great to meet earlier this week — thanks for the transparency around CloudStack's commercial. Per our call, I attached a concise option set that aligns with your budget target while protecting runtime SLAs and giving you a clean migration path. High level (see attached price_summary):

- Proposal A (Seat-first): fixed per-seat price with a 3-tier seat discount at 100 / 1k / 5k seats. Includes a 6-week free parallel pilot (no runtime charge), 30% migration credit applied as a one-time invoice credit after cutover.
- Proposal B (Consumption-first): per-inference token/compute model with aggressive volume breaks. Lower entry price but requires 60-day onboarding milestone to qualify for onboarding credits.
- Migration assistance: optional Dedicated capacity reservation during cutover (2 weeks) + up to 40 hrs of engineering hand-hold included in both proposals.
- Payment/term flexibility: 60-day net or prepay discount options listed in the sheet.

Jonas and I discussed leaning on a migration credit + pilot waiver rather than large flat discounts — it preserves run-rate economics and reduces rollback risk. That said, I'm prepared to match CloudStack's effective unit economics for the first 6 months if you confirm a 12-month commitment (we'll reflect that in a sideletter).

Attachments: packageloader_price_summary.xlsx, Packageloader_SOW_v1.pdf

Please review and tell me which structure you prefer (seat vs consumption) and any hard constraints on payment timing or legal language. If useful, we can sketch an itemized mutual action plan (MAP) and hand that to your procurement.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

---
[Attachment stub: packageloader_price_summary.xlsx (XLSX) — 4 tables: seat_breakdown, consumption_tiers, migration_credit, payment_options]
[Attachment stub: Packageloader_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF) — 3 pages: onboarding scope, responsibilities, timeline]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging & migration credits proposal for Packageloader — pricing alignment

Naomi — quick internal note:

- I like the pilot-waiver + migration-credit approach. It minimizes short-term revenue bleed and gives measurable milestones to trigger credits (good for finance).
- If they push for a price-match, counter with a time-bound effective-match: mirror competitor unit economics for months 0-6 in exchange for the 12-month commit Naomi proposed. Emphasize that the unit match is retroactive only up to the migration credit (so we don't over-index long-term footprint).
- Recommend we reserve the Dedicated burst (2 weeks) but make the engineering hand-hold explicit in SOW hours and deliverables — avoids open-ended scoping.
- Legal flag: procurement will likely ask for an SLA credit carveout and a one-way termination right if we materially miss the migration milestones. Ask Legal if we can accept a capped termination fee instead of broad T&Cs.

I'll backchannel with finance to see what concession levers we have (e.g., prepay breakpoints, short-term usage rebates) and loop legal on the termination language.

Jonas
VP, GTM Strategy (notes)
jonas.weber@redwood.com

---
Internal note only — please keep internal threads in Slack when this becomes negotiation via procurement.

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@packageloader.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@packageloader.com>, Mark Fisher <mark.fisher@packageloader.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging & migration credits proposal for Packageloader — pricing alignment

Naomi — thanks for sending this over. A few clarifying questions from procurement/engineering before we escalate to legal:

1) CloudStack gave us an effective unit price that is ~20% below our current run-rate for the first 6 months when you factor in their migration credit. Can Redwood match that effective 6-month unit economics if we sign a 12-month commitment? If yes, we need the math spelled out (line items).

2) Payment terms: Can we get net-90 for the first two invoices? Our finance team needs runway for the cutover month.

3) Migration window and rollback plan: We must preserve a two-week rollback window with minimal egress. What egress caps/credits would you provide if we exceed agreed egress during cutover?

4) References: please provide two similar-sized customers who completed a cross-vendor migration in the last 12 months and can speak to run-rate delta and time-to-stable.

Attaching the procurement RFP for context (PL_RFP_2027.pdf).

If you can confirm the effective match + terms above, we can draft a short sideletter and loop legal.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Partnerships
Packageloader Inc.
elena.rossi@packageloader.com

[Attachment stub: PL_RFP_2027.pdf (PDF) — procurement RFP, 8 pages]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@packageloader.com>
Cc: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@packageloader.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging & migration credits proposal for Packageloader — pricing alignment

Elena / Ben — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Effective 6-month match: Yes — we can match the competitor's effective unit economics for months 0–6 conditional on a 12-month minimum term. I've attached an annotated spreadsheet (see packageloader_price_summary.xlsx) with the math line-by-line: base unit, migration credit amortization, and billing cadence. Summary: the match reduces your effective unit price by ~18–22% depending on the seat mix.

2) Payment terms: We can accept net-90 for the first two invoices provided a signed MAP confirming cutover windows and a pre-authorized payment method on file. Finance will require the contract signature before activation.

3) Egress & rollback: We will include a one-time egress credit pool equal to 5% of projected monthly run-rate for the cutover month. If egress exceeds that pool, overages billed at normal rate but eligible for a goodwill credit if rollback occurs due to platform issues under Redwood's control. We'll enumerate conditions in the SOW.

4) References: I'll connect you to two customers (RetailOps and BeaconHealth) who completed switch projects in the last 10 months — I'll introduce you to their platform leads once you greenlight a reference call.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm which pricing structure you prefer (seat-first vs consumption-first) by EOD Wed.
- If seat-first, accept the annotated sideletter that mirrors effective-match months 0–6 + the migration credit.
- Once you confirm, I'll send a draft sideletter + DocuSign link for signature and loop Legal to confirm termination carveouts (Jonas is copied).

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.net/PL-2027-049-sign
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/PL-2027-049

Appreciate the collaborative tone — we want this to be low friction for your team.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
